# signal-smooth

Source: https://github.com/fushigivt/signal-smooth/blob/master/README.md

# signal-smooth

Frame-rate independent signal smoothing primitives for games and interactive applications.

`no_std` compatible. No allocations.

## Filters

- **`DampedSpring`** — Critically-damped spring. Smooth, non-oscillatory transitions controlled by a halflife parameter.
- **`Ema`** — Exponential moving average with frame-rate independent halflife.
- **`OneEuroFilter`** — Adaptive low-pass filter ([Casiez et al. 2012](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2207676.2208639)). Smooths jitter at rest, passes through fast motion with minimal lag.
- **`apply_deadzone`** / **`apply_deadzone_symmetric`** — Smoothstep and remapped deadzones for analog inputs.

## Usage

```toml
[dependencies]
signal-smooth = "0.1"
```

### Damped spring

```rust
use signal_smooth::DampedSpring;

let mut spring = DampedSpring::new(0.0);

// In your update loop:
let smoothed = spring.update(target, 0.1, dt); // halflife=0.1s
```

### Exponential moving average

```rust
use signal_smooth::Ema;

let mut ema = Ema::new(0.0);
let smoothed = ema.update(target, 0.15, dt); // halflife=0.15s
```

### 1-Euro filter

```rust
use signal_smooth::OneEuroFilter;

let mut filter = OneEuroFilter::new(1.0, 0.007); // min_cutoff, beta
let smoothed = filter.filter(noisy_value, dt);
```

### Deadzone

```rust
use signal_smooth::{apply_deadzone, apply_deadzone_symmetric};

let v = apply_deadzone(stick_x, 0.1);           // smoothstep fade
let v = apply_deadzone_symmetric(stick_x, 0.1); // remap to full range
```

## `no_std`

The crate is `no_std` by default. An optional `std` feature is available but currently unused.
